title: Field Echo Parsebook and Feature Batch (Q2 2026)
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc is a compact 'parsebook' of recent frontline vocal signals (support threads, CSM interviews, sales discovery notes, internal ops incidents) that converge on a small batch of candidate features and mitigations. Goal: give eng/product a prioritized, runnable set of asks with evidence, short-term patches, and potential metrics to track.

Data sources sampled (last 90 days):
- 18 support threads flagged as "latency tail" across hosted API & dedicated accounts (CS queue).
- 6 customer interviews (mid-market, regulated) focused on onboarding private deployments.
- 12 field bug reports mentioning KV-cache misses and repeated cold-start token spikes.
- Usage snapshots from Console: 4 customers reported unexpected token bill spikes tied to debugging loops.
- Two enterprise pilots reported embedding drift (semantic mismatch) after model upgrades.

Representative customer quotes (anonymized):
- "We saw a 3x median latency on burst days and had to reduce concurrency to stay under SLA — costly for throughput."
- "Private deployment onboarding took our infra team three weeks to wire up KMS and network routes; the docs didn't map to our VPN topology."
- "After you rolled the new quantized variant, our reranker started returning worse relevance for short queries."

Top emergent themes (high-level):
1) Latency tail events and cold cache penalty — recurring impact on customer SLAs.
2) Private onboarding friction — networking, KMS, and observability gaps.
3) Cost surprises during debug/looping requests — billing granularity & token attribution blindspots.
4) Model upgrade regressions (rerank/embedding drift) — need eval hooks tied to rollouts.
5) API ergonomics around streaming resumability / function-calling consistency.

Patch-to-product map (prioritized):
- Quick wins (2–4 weeks):
  * Add a console telemetry flag and alert template for "KV-cache cold-start rate" (owner: Maya; impact: quick visibility to CS/SE).
  * Billing debug mode: per-request sampling of token attribution + annotated examples for customers (owner: Finance-API; impact: reduces SRE/CS triage time).
  * Onboarding checklist: network topology templates (AWS VPC, GCP-VPC-SC, Azure) + KMS quickstart script for private (owner: Solutions Eng).
- Medium (1–3 months):
  * Graceful fallback policy for hosted -> compatible lower-capacity model variant when latency SLOs degrade (owner: Serving Runtime; impact: reliability improvement).
  * Rollback-safe model-eval harness integrated into rollouts that runs customer-provided prompt sets (owner: Product/Optimize).
  * Streaming resumability spec: SDK-side checkpointing + server-side token-offset resume (owner: DevX).
- Strategic (3–6+ months):
  * KV-cache prefetching heuristics + per-tenant cache warmup during scheduled rollouts (owner: Serving Runtime + Infra).
  * Billing UI rework: session-scoped cost breakdowns and debug export (owner: Console).
  * Private deployer: automated KMS & routing validator (preflight) that emits concrete remediation hints (owner: Private Deployments).

Prioritization rationale (scoring):
- Scoring axis: frequency (how many customers), intensity (impact on revenue/SLAs), tractability (engineering effort).
- Quick wins rank highest because they lower CS/SE triage and reduce churn risk. Fallback + eval harness are high-frequency, high-intensity items that protect Enterprise customers during rollouts.

Risk flags and tradeoffs:
- Fallback to lower-capacity model may hide quality degradations; must be coupled with A/B and automated alerts so product teams can track downstream user-impact.
- Automated KV prefetching increases memory pressure on shared pools; needs capacity tests and a per-tenant throttle policy.
- Billing debug mode will expose sensitive usage traces — must filter PII and obey retention/KMS policies.

Evidence snippets (attachments / examples):
- Support thread CS-8701: attached timing histograms showing tail latency at 95th/99th percentiles correlated with concurrent cache-misses.
- Pilot notes (Enterprise F): prompt set that regressed after model patch: {short product names -> lower rerank score}.
- Onboarding timeline: Org X took 21 days; breakdown: 9 days networking, 6 days KMS, 6 days test & validation.

Proposed KPI dashboard (small set to track after releases):
- KV-cache cold-start rate by tenant (daily)
- 95th & 99th latency for typical seq lengths (per model)
- Number of private onboarding support hours (CS logged) per customer
- Post-rollout retrieval/embedding QA delta (avg similarity drop on seeded prompts)

Suggested owners and initial asks:
- Serving Runtime: investigate lightweight per-tenant warmup + fallback policy prototype (ask: allocate 1 sprint).
- DevX (SDK): draft streaming resumability RFC + sample implementation for Node/Python (ask: spike).
- Console: create KV cold-start alert + billing debug export (ask: 2-week patch).
- Solutions Eng / Private Deployments: consolidate KMS/networking onboarding checklist and run two 1:1 pilot migrations with templated preflight (ask: schedule).

Immediate next steps (this week):
1) Triage meeting with owners (Serving Runtime, Console, DevX, Solutions Eng) to align on quick wins and owners — target: Tues 2026-06-15.
2) Create shared test prompt set and privacy-scrubbed telemetry export for the two impacted pilots; upload to Confluence.
3) CS to add KV-cache cold-start alert to three flagged customer accounts as a temporary monitoring measure.

Open questions for product/eng: 
- What are the memory/cost constraints for tenant prefetching on Dedicated vs Hosted?
- Can rollout eval harness run in a sandbox mode for private deployments without leaking data to hosted evaluation services?
- What PCI/PHI constraints do we need to bake into billing debug exports?

Appendix: quick wins playbook (step-by-step):
- KV cold-start alert:
  1) Console: add metric (cache_miss_rate_per_request) tag by tenant in telemetry pipeline.
  2) Alert: firing when >5% cold-starts over 5m window at p95 traffic.
  3) CS: on alert, open support ticket with cold-start histogram & suggested mitigations (reduce max_seq, increase cache TTL).
- Billing debug export:
  1) Sample 1% of requests for full attribution; redact input text fields, preserve token counts & model variant.
  2) Provide customers a one-click export link valid for 24h with owner approval.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact; the focus is on executable asks rather than exhaustive signal. Please annotate any missing customer examples you know of and flag owners who should be added.

Prepared by: Sofia Thompson (CS); draft for internal review.
